concept.name: Managed money
concept.definition: A trader category in the CFTC's Disaggregated Commitments of Traders report comprising registered commodity trading advisors (CTAs), registered commodity pool operators (CPOs), and unregistered funds identified by the CFTC — traders engaged in managing and conducting organized futures trading on behalf of clients.
concept.intuition: It is the 'fund money' line in the COT report: positions run by professional managers trading other people's capital.
concept.mechanics: CFTC staff assign reportable traders to the category using Form 40 data and other information, based on predominant activity; hedge funds are included regardless of registration status. Managed money open interest is reported long, short, and spreading, where spreading is computed from offsetting positions in different calendar months of the same or related contracts.
concept.failure_modes: Classification is at the trader level, so a fund's hedge-like spread books and directional books are aggregated; the spreading column partially offsets but residual judgment remains. Unregistered and offshore funds are identified only where the CFTC can identify them, so coverage is not perfectly complete.
concept.misconceptions: Managed money is not synonymous with all speculators — other reportables also speculate; nor is it the same as the legacy noncommercial category, which also included non-fund speculators. Managed-money net length is a positioning fact, not evidence of informed forecasting skill.
concept.example: A CPO operating a commodity pool with a large long in gold futures is classified as managed money; its position appears in the Disaggregated COT's managed money long column each week.
